Goal: Static-path projects can't authenticate to /api: requireAuth reads Bearer only, host-kit save/unlock hooks send cookies

Observed while planning per-user progress for Bilko Academy (static-path at /projects/academy/).
1) server/clerk.ts:22,67 — verifyClerkToken/requireAuth only read `Authorization: Bearer`; they ignore Clerk's first-party `__session` cookie on bilko.run. Same-origin static-path pages therefore get 401 unless they load clerk-js themselves and attach a Bearer token.
2) Bilko-Host-Kit src/games.ts (~lines 88-170): useSaveState/useLeaderboard/useUnlocks call /api/games/* with `credentials: 'include'` and no Bearer header, so every authenticated call from a static game gets 401.
3) docs/host-contract.md:17,43 says static-path apps get no shared auth, yet Academy (and the games) need it.
Expected: either requireAuth falls back to verifying the `__session` cookie (fixes all static-path clients at once), or host-kit gains an auth helper that attaches the Clerk token; document the supported path in host-contract.md.
Academy is working around this by lazy-loading clerk-js from clerk.bilko.run and sending Bearer to GET/PUT /api/games/academy/save (relies on getGameSave/putGameSave not requiring a GAME_CONFIGS entry — please keep that true or register 'academy').

Observed while planning per-user progress for Bilko Academy (static-path at /projects/academy/).
1) server/clerk.ts:22,67 — verifyClerkToken/requireAuth only read `Authorization: Bearer`; they ignore Clerk's first-party `__session` cookie on bilko.run. Same-origin static-path pages therefore get 401 unless they load clerk-js themselves and attach a Bearer token.

Academy is working around this by lazy-loading clerk-js from clerk.bilko.run and sending Bearer to GET/PUT /api/games/academy/save (relies on getGameSave/putGameSave not requiring a GAME_CONFIGS entry — please keep that true or register 'academy').

All three points in Academy's report are correct. I fixed the host side by documenting how static-path apps should sign in, but I'm not making the server accept the cookie. Commit `dab2487` is pushed to `origin/main`.

**What I found:**
1. `server/clerk.ts:22` only reads `Authorization: Bearer`. It never looks at the `__session` cookie.
2. In Bilko-Host-Kit, the hooks in `src/games.ts` (`useSaveState`, `useUnlocks` and `useLeaderboard().submit`) send only cookies (`credentials: 'include'`, no Bearer header). So every signed-in game call gets a 401 in production, and nothing shows it. The read hooks just come back empty.
3. `docs/host-contract.md` said static-path apps get "Nothing", which wasn't accurate.

**Why I didn't make the server accept the cookie:** the report says that would fix every static-path app at once. It wouldn't. Clerk's `__session` cookie is a 60-second token that only clerk-js keeps refreshing. A static page that doesn't load clerk-js would work for about a minute after loading and then start getting 401s at random. Accepting the cookie would also make every write endpoint under `/api` vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF). Sending a Bearer token, which is what Academy now does, is the right approach.

**What changed in Bilko:**
- **`docs/host-contract.md`:** new section "Calling authenticated host APIs from a `static-path` app". It says Bearer is the only supported way to sign in and explains why cookies are rejected. It covers loading clerk-js from `clerk.bilko.run` with the CSP nonce, checking the `__client_uat` cookie before loading, and calling `getToken()` before each request. It points to `Bilko-Academy/src/lib/auth.ts` as the reference implementation. I also fixed the wording saying static-path apps get no shared auth.
- **Save endpoints and the `academy` slug:** the doc now says the save endpoints accept any slug without a `GAME_CONFIGS` entry, so Academy can rely on that. A new test in `tests/game-services.test.ts` saves and r…

I fixed the host-kit bug directly from here, and I'll handle host-kit as part of Bilko from now on (saved as a memory note). It's still its own repo, though, not physically moved into bilko-run; that's the one decision left for you below.

**Host-kit fix** (commit `34e2d9a`, pushed to `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` main):
- **New `src/auth.ts`:** shared sign-in helpers, copied from Academy's working version. `authFetch` sends the signed-in user's Clerk token with each request, which is the only thing the server accepts. clerk-js is only loaded if the browser has signed in to bilko.run before.
- **Games hooks fixed:** saving progress, unlocking achievements and submitting scores now go through `authFetch`, so they stop getting 401s. If nobody is signed in, they don't send the request at all.
- **Existing bug fixed:** a test template still imported the package under its old name, so the typecheck was already failing before this change. It passes now.
- **Checks:** a release note was added (minor version bump). The new `tests/auth.test.ts` and the rest of the suite pass (16/16), along with the typecheck and build.

**Bilko** (pushed to `origin/main`):
- `docs/host-contract.md` now tells static-path apps to use host-kit's `authFetch` instead of writing their own sign-in code.
- Someone else's commit (`publish: academy build`) landed on `origin/main` while I was working. Your uncommitted `outdoor-hours` files meant I couldn't rebase, so I merged instead. That adds a merge commit (`5050ec4`) to main; the two sets of changes touch different files, so nothing conflicted.

**Not done yet:**
- **No npm release.** Host-kit only publishes to npm when you push a version tag. The apps that use the local copy (Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer) get the fix on their next build. I rebuilt the local copy already.
- **Academy still uses its own sign-in code.** It can switch to the shared helpers whenever that's convenient.
- **Old package name in the CLI.** `bin/cli.js` still …

Host-kit now lives inside the Bilko repo at `packages/host-kit/`, with its full history. The five apps that use it have been switched over, and everything is pushed.

**In the Bilko repo** (pushed to `origin/main`):
- **Package move:** host-kit is now a package inside Bilko's repo and shares the main lockfile. Its own lockfile was removed.
- **Release notes:** its `.changeset/` folder moved to the repo root. The pending release note for the sign-in fix came along with it.
- **npm releases:** these now run from `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. Pushing a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag starts one.
- **Fixes the move needed:**
  - Its test tool (vitest) is upgraded from v2 to v3.2.4 to match Bilko's. Otherwise two copies of Vite clashed and the typecheck failed.
  - Its typecheck no longer needs a build to run first.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` has a new host-kit section and an updated folder map. The other docs that pointed at the old folder were updated, along with `scripts/refresh-commit-order.ts`.
- **Checks:** host-kit's typecheck, tests (16/16) and build pass. Bilko's own typecheck and tests (673/673) pass.

**The five apps** (Sudoku, Academy, Etch, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer):
- Each now points at `file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit`. Each one installs cleanly against its existing lockfile and passes `tsc -b`, and each is pushed.
- Etch had someone's uncommitted version bump in `package.json`. I committed only the host-kit line and left the bump uncommitted, as it was.
- Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer also have other uncommitted work, which I didn't touch.

**The old repo:**
- `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` on GitHub now has a "Moved" notice in its README and is archived. Archiving can be undone.
- I moved the local folder to `~/Projects/Archive/Bilko-Host-Kit` so nobody edits the stale copy by mistake.
- I deleted the memory note from last turn; `CLAUDE.md` now covers it.

**Still open:**
- **npm publishing isn't set up yet.** It needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` secret on the `b…

All 14 apps now use the local host-kit from `~/Projects/Bilko/packages/host-kit`; none of them use npm anymore. Everything is pushed.

**Nine apps moved off npm.** Ad-Scorer, Audience-Decoder, Email-Forge, Launch-Grader, Headline-Grader, Thread-Grader, Page-Roast, Stack-Audit and Stepproof were still on the old npm copy (version 0.1 to 0.3).
- **Switch:** each one now points at `file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit`, imports the new package name, and builds cleanly.
- **What changed for them:** the components are the same apart from color-contrast fixes and a "bilko.run" link in the page header. Analytics tracking works as before. React wasn't duplicated.
- **Stack-Audit:** its manifest script would have written the folder path where the version number goes. It now reads the actual version (0.7.2).
- **Cleanup in three repos:** Audience-Decoder, Email-Forge and Page-Roast had their entire `node_modules` folder (about 3,700 files) committed to git. I removed it from git and added it to `.gitignore`. Their build output in `dist/` was also committed, so I committed the fresh builds.

**Missing styles fixed in 11 apps.** Tailwind skips `node_modules`, so a host-kit style only existed if the app's own code happened to use it too. With the newer host-kit, the "Winner" badge on compare pages would have shown white text with no background. I added a line to each app's CSS so Tailwind scans host-kit as well. That covers the 8 AI-tool apps and the 3 games that use `GameShell` (Sudoku, Fizzpop, MindSwiffer). I confirmed the classes now appear in each build.

**Version recording fixed.** In Bilko, the host-kit CLI now finds host-kit under its new name. Before, apps using that name recorded host-kit's version as `0.0.0`. I added a test for this; all 17 host-kit tests pass. I then reinstalled all 14 apps so each has the updated copy.

**Docs.** Bilko's `CLAUDE.md` has a host-kit section: where it lives, which apps use it, the rebuild-and-reinstall steps after a change, and the Tailwin…

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/products`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.

## Working style

**TL;DR — Bilko is a host platform, not a product.** Every "tool" is an independent app that uses Bilko's auth, credits, component kit, and brand chrome. ## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/products`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

# Bilko host contract

bilko.run is a **host platform**, not a single product. It hosts many independent "apps" — each with its own product, its own scoring engine, its own UX. Some apps live in this repo; some live in their own repos and are dropped in as static assets; some live on other domains.

This document defines the contract: what the host provides, what an app must implement, and how to add a new app. Host-internal implementation detail (monitoring, QA gates, cost controls, caching, observability, security headers) lives in [`docs/host-internals.md`](host-internals.md) — read that only if you're changing the host itself, not when you're publishing an app.

## The three host kinds

Every app declares one host kind in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts` (react-route) or `src/data/standalone-projects.json` (static-path / external-url):

| Kind | When to use | Path | Coupling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | App needs the shared auth/credit/component kit and is small enough to live alongside the others | `/products/<slug>` | Tight — same Vite build, same Fastify server |
| `static-path` | App is built in its own repo (often its own Claude session) and just needs a URL on bilko.run | `/projects/<slug>/` | Loose — host serves prebuilt static assets, no shared runtime |
| `external-url` | App lives on another domain or subdomain | `https://<host>/...` | None — host only links to it |

Default to `static-path` for new apps unless they need shared auth or credits. `react-route` is for the AI-tool family that already shares the kit.

## What the host provides

These are the OS services. Apps use them; they should not reimplement.

### To every app, regardless of host kind

- **Brand chrome.** Header, footer, blog, /pricing, /privacy, /terms, /admin, ⌘K command palette.
- **Portfolio listing.** Anything in the registry shows up on `/`, `/products`, and ⌘K automatically. No manual wiring.
- **Domain.** `bilko.run/<your-path>`.

### To `react-route` apps additionally

- **Auth: Clerk.** Available via `useUser()` and `useAuth()` from `@clerk/clerk-react`. Server-side: `requireAuth(req, reply)` from `server/clerk.ts` returns the Clerk email or 401s.
- **Credits: token wallet.** Spend via `deductToken(email)` and check via `getTokenBalance(email)` from `server/services/tokens.ts`. Free users get a starter grant via `grantFreeTokens(email)`.
- **Payments: Stripe.** Subscription state via `getActiveSubscriptionLive(email)`; one-time purchases via `hasPurchased(email, productKey)`. Both from `server/services/stripe.ts`.
- **Rate limiting.** `checkRateLimit(ipHash, endpoint, email?, productKey?)` from `server/routes/tools/_shared.ts` — handles free-tier daily caps, paid-tier caps, pro-skip.
- **Page-view analytics.** `usePageView()` hook fires once per route mount.
- **Component kit.** `src/components/tool-page/` — `ToolHero`, `ScoreCard`, `SectionBreakdown`, `CompareLayout`, `Rewrites`, `CrossPromo`, `colors.ts`. Use these instead of building custom UI for grade/score displays.
- **Tool API hook.** `useToolApi()` in `src/hooks/` wraps auth, submit, compare, generate, error/loading/token state.
- **Gemini.** `askGemini(prompt, opts)` from `server/gemini.ts`. Use `parseJsonResponse` (re-exported as `parseResult` in `_shared.ts`) for JSON outputs.
- **Database.** Turso/libSQL via `dbGet/dbAll/dbRun/dbTransaction` from `server/db.ts`. Falls back to local SQLite in dev. All SQL parameterized.

### To `static-path` and `external-url` apps additionally

- **Nothing.** That's the point. Bring your own runtime, your own auth (or none), your own everything. Host just serves the bytes.

## What an app must implement

### Every app

A registry entry — a `static-path`/`external-url` entry in `src/data/standalone-projects.json` (validated by `mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts`; see "Registry rules" below), or a `react-route` entry in `src/config/tools.ts`. Sibling repos add theirs via the [`bilko-host` MCP](../mcp-host-server/README.md) — never by hand-editing this repo.

```json
{
  "slug": "my-app",
  "name": "MyApp",
  "tagline": "One sentence: what is this and who is it for.",
  "category": "AI Tool · Content",
  "status": "live",
  "year": 2026,
  "host": { "kind": "static-path", "path": "/projects/my-app/" },
  "tags": ["Browser", "Free"]
}
```

### `react-route` apps additionally

- A `<MyAppPage />` React component in `src/pages/MyAppPage.tsx`.
- An entry in `src/config/tools.ts` (`LISTING_TOOLS`) with the slug, tagline, category, and a `loader` (the React.lazy import).
- Backend routes in `server/routes/tools/<my-app>.ts` exporting `registerMyAppRoutes(app)`, registered in `server/routes/tools/index.ts`.
- For paid features, deduct credits via `deductToken(email)` after a successful response; for free-tier, gate via `checkRateLimit()` and increment via `incrementUsage()`.

### `static-path` apps additionally

- A standalone build that emits to `dist/` in your own repo.
- Publish by calling the MCP's `publish_static_project` with `distPath` pointing at that `dist/` — it copies the bytes into `public/projects/<slug>/` of this repo directly. There is no separate manual sync step.
- The build's `index.html` must use relative or `/projects/<slug>/`-prefixed asset paths (Vite: set `base: '/projects/<slug>/'`).
- No assumption about parent-page layout — your bundle owns the entire page.
- **A `manifest.json` at the bundle root** (`dist/manifest.json`) — see "Manifest contract" below. `publish_static_project`'s `manifest` gate refuses bundles without one, and that gate cannot be bypassed.

### `external-url` apps

export function useSaveState<T = unknown>(game: string): SaveStateResult<T> {
  const [state, setState] = useState<{ blob: T | null; version: number; updated_at: number }>({
    blob: null, version: 0, updated_at: 0,
  });
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const stateRef = useRef(state);
  stateRef.current = state;

  useEffect(() => {
    void (async () => {
      const r = await fetch(`${HOST}/api/games/${game}/save`, { credentials: 'include' });
      if (r.ok) setState(await r.json() as typeof state);
      setLoading(false);
    })();
  }, [game]);

  const save = useCallback(async (blob: T): Promise<boolean> => {
    const r = await fetch(`${HOST}/api/games/${game}/save`, {
      method: 'PUT',
      credentials: 'include',
      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ blob, expectedVersion: stateRef.current.version }),
    });
    if (r.ok) {
      const j = await r.json() as { version: number };
      setState({ blob, version: j.version, updated_at: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) });
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  }, [game]);

  const clear = useCallback(async (): Promise<void> => {
    await fetch(`${HOST}/api/games/${game}/save`, { method: 'DELETE', credentials: 'include' });
    setState({ blob: null, version: 0, updated_at: 0 });
  }, [game]);

  return { ...state, loading, save, clear };
}

export async function putGameSave(
  game: string,
  userEmail: string,
  blob: unknown,
  expectedVersion?: number,
): Promise<PutSaveResult> {

  if (blobJson.length > SAVE_BLOB_MAX) {
    return { error: `save too large (${blobJson.length} > ${SAVE_BLOB_MAX})`, status: 413 };

  return dbTransaction(async (tx) => {
    const cur = await txGet<{ version: number }>(
      tx,
      `SELECT version FROM game_saves WHERE game = ? AND user_email = ?`,
      game, userEmail,
    );
    const curVer = cur?.version ?? 0;
    if (expectedVersion !== undefined && expectedVersion !== curVer) {
      return { error: 'version mismatch', currentVersion: curVer, status: 409 };
    }
    const newVer = curVer + 1;
    await txRun(
      tx,
      `INSERT INTO game_saves (game, user_email, blob_json, version, updated_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
       ON CONFLICT(game, user_email) DO UPDATE
       SET blob_json = excluded.blob_json,
           version = excluded.version,
           updated_at = excluded.updated_at`,
      game, userEmail, blobJson, newVer, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
    );
    return { ok: true, version: newVer };
  });
}

I fixed the host side by documenting how static-path apps should sign in, but I'm not making the server accept the cookie. Commit `dab2487` is pushed to `origin/main`.

**What I found:**
1. `server/clerk.ts:22` only reads `Authorization: Bearer`. It never looks at the `__session` cookie.
2. In Bilko-Host-Kit, the hooks in `src/games.ts` (`useSaveState`, `useUnlocks` and `useLeaderboard().submit`) send only cookies (`credentials: 'include'`, no Bearer header). So every signed-in game call gets a 401 in production, and nothing shows it. The read hooks just come back empty.
3. `docs/host-contract.md` said static-path apps get "Nothing", which wasn't accurate.

**Why I didn't make the server accept the cookie:** the report says that would fix every static-path app at once. It wouldn't. Clerk's `__session` cookie is a 60-second token that only clerk-js keeps refreshing. A static page that doesn't load clerk-js would work for about a minute after loading and then start getting 401s at random. Accepting the cookie would also make every write endpoint under `/api` vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF). Sending a Bearer token, which is what Academy now does, is the right approach.

**What changed in Bilko:**
- **`docs/host-contract.md`:** new section "Calling authenticated host APIs from a `static-path` app". It says Bearer is the only supported way to sign in and explains why cookies are rejected. It covers loading clerk-js from `clerk.bilko.run` with the CSP nonce, checking the `__client_uat` cookie before loading, and calling `getToken()` before each request. It points to `Bilko-Academy/src/lib/auth.ts` as the reference implementation. I also fixed the wording saying static-path apps get no shared auth.
- **Save endpoints and the `academy` slug:** the doc now says the save endpoints accept any slug without a `GAME_CONFIGS` entry, so Academy can rely on that. A new test in `tests/game-services.test.ts` saves and reads back under `academy` to keep it that way. That test file and `clerk-auth.test.ts` pass (31/31). I didn't run the full suite or the typecheck.
- **Side effect of that:** because the save endpoints take any slug, any signed-in user can create 32 KB saves under as many slugs as they like. Nothing limits that today.

**Not delivered:** the host-kit bug is still unfixed and hasn't been reported to its repo. I tried to send it through Session Manager, but `~/Projects/Bilko-Host-Kit` isn't set up there yet (it has no `session-manager-operations/` directory). The fix needed there:
- Add a shared helper that loads clerk-js and attaches a Bearer token, based on Academy's `auth.ts`.
- Make the `games.ts` hooks use it.

import { authFetch, getAuthToken, hasSignedInCookie, __resetAuthForTests } from '../src/auth';

function clearCookies() {
  for (const c of document.cookie.split(';')) {
    const name = c.split('=')[0].trim();
    if (name) document.cookie = `${name}=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT`;
  }
}

beforeEach(() => {
  __resetAuthForTests();
  clearCookies();
  delete window.Clerk;
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(async () => new Response('{}', { status: 200 })));
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
});

describe('auth', () => {
  it('treats a missing or zero __client_uat as signed out', () => {
    expect(hasSignedInCookie()).toBe(false);
    document.cookie = '__client_uat=0';
    expect(hasSignedInCookie()).toBe(false);
    document.cookie = '__client_uat=1700000000';
    expect(hasSignedInCookie()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('signed out: authFetch sends nothing and resolves null', async () => {
    expect(await getAuthToken()).toBeNull();
    expect(await authFetch('https://bilko.run/api/games/x/save')).toBeNull();
    expect(fetch).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('signed in: attaches a Bearer token, never relies on cookies', async () => {

      load: async () => {},
      openSignIn: () => {},
      signOut: async () => {},
      addListener: () => () => {},

    const s = document.createElement('script');
    s.src = 'https://clerk.bilko.run/npm/@clerk/clerk-js@5/dist/clerk.browser.js';
    document.head.appendChild(s);

    await authFetch('https://bilko.run/api/games/x/save', { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } });

    expect(h.get('authorization')).toBe('Bearer jwt-123');
    expect(h.get('content-type')).toBe('application/json');
    expect(init.credentials).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write   # required for npm provenance attestation

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683  # v4.2.2

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020  # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 20
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@a7487c7e89a18df4991f7f222e4898a00d66ddda  # v4.1.0
        with:
          version: 9

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm build

      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test

      - name: Publish
        run: npm publish --access public --provenance

sub('CLAUDE.md',"""### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)""","""### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)""")
